# Review of FDS 6.2 Tank Pressure Control

## Defect list

| # | Clause | Defect | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.2.3 | **High-high pressure trips the compressors.** The BOG compressors are the main way to reduce tank pressure. Tripping them at the highest pressure removes pressure relief just when it is needed, and the "protect them" rationale is unsupported because the compressors see low suction pressure here. A tank PAHH should stop pressure sources (close LNG inlet/fill valves, stop unloading, stop any heat input), not remove relief capacity. Compressor protection belongs on the compressors' own suction/discharge/temperature/vibration trips. | Critical |
| 2 | 6.2.4 | **HMI bypass of a protective trip.** A software bypass from the HMI defeats a safety function with no authorization, time limit, alarm or independence from the BPCS. Maintenance bypass should be per transmitter within a voting scheme, controlled by a permit and key/hardwired switch, time-limited, and alarmed. | Critical |
| 3 | 6.2.5 | **Low pressure is dismissed.** Pressure control does not prevent vacuum. BOG generation falls (idle, atmospheric pressure rise, no unloading) while compressors run continuously, and the tank can be pulled down. A full-containment tank has very little vacuum margin (here -5 mbarg). No PAL, PALL, minimum-flow/recycle, compressor low-suction trip or make-up gas is defined. | Critical |
| 4 | 6.2.6 | **Vacuum relief admits air.** Air ingress into an LNG tank creates a flammable mixture and freezes moisture. The vacuum breaker should be fed from a fuel gas/NG make-up source, with air only as a last resort that is explicitly justified. | High |
| 5 | 6.2.6 | **PSV set at 290 mbarg with no stated design pressure.** If 290 mbarg is the tank design pressure, relieving at 290 plus accumulation exceeds design. There is no sizing basis (fire, rollover, flash, loss of compressors with maximum BOG, N+1 valves) and no discharge location. | High |
| 6 | 6.2.7 | **Anti-surge is delegated with no interface.** Anti-surge only applies if the compressors are centrifugal, and the compressor type is not stated. The interface is undefined: recycle path and cooling, valve fail position, interaction with PIC-501 capacity control and minimum flow, and which signals the vendor exposes. | High |
| 7 | 6.2.1 | **Control philosophy is incomplete.** It does not state how capacity is varied (speed, suction throttle, recycle, unloading), the turndown and minimum flow, duty/standby arrangement (2x100%? 2x50%?) or auto-start of the standby. It does not say where the BOG goes (send-out, fuel gas, recondenser, flare) or how discharge pressure is controlled. | Medium |
| 8 | 6.2.2 | **Flare valve action is underspecified.** There is no valve fail position, close/reset setpoint or hysteresis, so it can cycle and flare the tank down into the compressor control band. Valve response and flare capacity vs. loss-of-compressor BOG are not stated. | Medium |
| 9 | 6.2.2 / 6.2.3 | **Transmitter independence is not stated.** Control (PIC-501/510), alarm and trip functions need separate transmitters, with 2oo3 voting for SIS. There are no PAH or PAL alarms and no tag numbers for the trip (e.g. PSHH). | Medium |
| 10 | General | **Missing items.** There is no reset/restart logic after trips, no operating modes (holding, unloading, send-out) with their BOG loads, and no setpoint ladder showing the order of actions. | Medium |

## Corrected section

All numbers in [brackets] are proposals to be confirmed against the tank design basis (design pressure, design vacuum), the HAZOP/LOPA and the compressor data sheet.

**6.2 Tank Pressure Control**

**6.2.1 Normal control**
- PIC-501 shall maintain tank pressure at [120] mbarg by modulating the capacity of the duty BOG compressor (K-501A or K-501B) via [speed / suction throttle / unloading, per vendor]. The standby compressor shall auto-start on duty compressor trip or when the duty is at maximum capacity for more than [x] min.
- Compressor arrangement: [2x100% / 2x50%]. BOG discharge shall go to [send-out header / fuel gas / recondenser], with discharge pressure controlled by [PIC-xxx].
- The compressors shall not be required to run continuously. They shall operate between minimum flow (with recycle if needed) and maximum capacity, and shall stop on a controlled low-pressure condition (6.2.5).

**6.2.2 High-pressure relief to flare**
- PIC-510, using a transmitter separate from PIC-501's, shall open PV-512 to flare from [220] mbarg, with PV-512 fully open at [240] mbarg. PV-512 shall close at [205] mbarg (hysteresis) and shall fail [open/closed, per flare study]. Flare and PV-512 capacity shall cover maximum BOG with both compressors unavailable.
- Alarms: PAH at [180] mbarg and PAHH at [250] mbarg.

**6.2.3 High-high pressure protection (SIS)**
- PAHH-[xxx] at [250] mbarg (2oo3 transmitters, independent of BPCS) shall close the tank LNG inlet/fill valves and stop unloading and any LNG pump recirculation that adds heat. It shall **not** trip the BOG compressors. They shall continue to run, and PV-512 shall remain available to flare.
- Compressors shall be protected by their own trips (suction low pressure, discharge high pressure/temperature, vibration, seal gas), defined in the compressor package specification.
- Reset shall be manual, local, and only after pressure is below [200] mbarg.

**6.2.4 Bypasses**
- No SIS trip shall be bypassable from the HMI. A maintenance bypass shall be per transmitter (the remaining voting stays active), enabled by a key switch under a work permit. It shall be time-limited to [x] h, alarmed, and logged.

**6.2.5 Low-pressure and vacuum protection**
- PAL at [70] mbarg shall alarm. Below the PIC-501 setpoint, the compressor shall unload to minimum flow/recycle.
- Make-up: PIC-503 shall admit NG/fuel gas to the tank vapor space at [50] mbarg to hold the pressure.
- PALL-[xxx] at [30] mbarg (2oo3, SIS) shall trip the running BOG compressors and block BOG suction. Restart shall be inhibited until the pressure is above [60] mbarg.

**6.2.6 Overpressure and vacuum relief devices**
- Tank design pressure is [xxx] mbarg and design vacuum is [-xx] mbarg. PSVs shall be set at or below design pressure, sized for the governing case (fire, rollover, flash, loss of compressors with maximum BOG), with N+1 installed spares and discharge to [safe location / vent stack]. The nominal set pressure is [290] mbarg only if it is at or below design pressure.
- Vacuum relief valves shall be set at [-5] mbarg and shall draw from the NG/fuel gas make-up source. Air admission shall be used only if justified in the HAZOP, with the flammable-mixture risk addressed.

**6.2.7 Compressor anti-surge interface**
- The compressor type shall be [centrifugal/reciprocating/screw]. If anti-surge is applicable, the vendor package shall provide anti-surge control with a fail-open recycle valve and cooler, and shall expose to the DCS: surge margin, recycle valve position, compressor status/trip, and minimum-flow limit. PIC-501 capacity control shall not request flow below the vendor minimum, and its output shall be limited by the vendor package.

**6.2.8 Setpoint ladder (summary)**

| Pressure (mbarg) | Action |
|---|---|
| -5 | Vacuum relief (from NG make-up) |
| [30] | PALL: trip compressors (SIS) |
| [50] | Make-up gas admitted |
| [70] | PAL |
| [120] | PIC-501 control setpoint |
| [180] | PAH |
| [220–240] | PV-512 opens to flare |
| [250] | PAHH: close inlets/stop unloading (SIS) |
| ≤ design (≈[290]) | PSVs |
